answer: Velvet Threshold Nonce. Each new identity must submit a unique proof-of-work nonce whose hash also encodes a pigment tag derived from a shared random inlet seed published per epoch. Enforcement: the tag narrows the valid nonce space by 2^k; a clone reusing its parent’s tag finds valid nonces 2^k times scarcer, so marginal registration cost scales superlinearly with near-duplicate tags. An attacker pays 2^k extra compute per clone, making the marginal clone strictly negative-EV once k exceeds the value of one identity’s expected rewards.
